proposals.evidence: CDIAL 13161 saptāha period of seven days supports the pt-retaining Bengali/Hajong śopta week forms as learned Sanskrit vocabulary. Vowel rounding and the possible Bengali intermediary into Hajong are retained without requiring a settled intra-Indo-Aryan route. Exact survey form śopta is preserved.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 11242 vatsara gives Assamese basar and Bengali bachar year in the addenda. Hajong bośor fits this eastern year family; the sibilant and vowels are retained, and Turner himself leaves learned transmission possible. Exact survey form bośor is preserved.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 9964 mahiṣa gives regional mhes/mɔĩś buffalo, Hindi mhaĩs and neighboring maĩś forms. Goj mes/mēs, Kaithal mẽs and Hajong moiś are compared with this buffalo family; vowel, sibilant, nasal and aspiration details remain explicit and intra-Indo-Aryan transmission is open. Exact survey form moi̯ś is preserved.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 9917 maśaka gives Bengali maśā, Oriya masā and Maithili mos mosquito. Hajong and Adivasi Oriya mosa match this eastern mosquito family with the source vowels and sibilants retained. Exact survey form mosa is preserved.
